newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court declines to block Conrail vote.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court declines to block Conrail vote.

text.p: A federal appeals court panel Wednesday rejected a request by Norfolk Southern Corp. to block a meeting Friday at which Conrail shareholders are to vote on a key step in a planned $9.2 billion merger with CSX Corp.
The three-judge panel of the U.S. Third Circuit Court of Appeals issued its denial about one hour after hearing oral arguments on the request.

Norfolk Southern, whose $10.3 billion bid for Conrail has been rejected, was seeking to block the meeting pending its appeal of a lower court decision rejecting its challenges of provisions in the Conrail-CSX merger agreement.
It was the latest in a string of defeats for Norfolk Southern. Last week a federal judge and a regulatory agency denied Norfolk Southern's attempt to block the Conrail-CSX deal.

Norfolk Southern reiterated at the hearing its arguments that a two-year "exclusivity" provision in the merger agreement could coerce Conrail shareholders into approving the deal, which Norfolk Southern says was inferior to its own rival offer.
It also argued in court that Richmond, Va.-based CSX had already triggered a Pennsylvania law that would require it to pay all cash for Conrail.

At the meeting, Conrail will be asking shareholders to waive the Pennsylvania law that would essentially require CSX to pay for Conrail in cash. The proposed Conrail-CSX transaction is a mixture of cash and stock.
Norfolk Southern has publicly urged Conrail shareholders to reject the deal.
Norfolk, Va.-based Norfolk Southern said late Monday it would buy 9.9 percent of Conrail stock if the Philadelphia-based railroad's shareholders defeated the measure to waive the law.

Conrail and CSX argued in Wednesday's hearing that Norfolk Southern had provided no factual evidence in the lower court case on which to base an appeal, and said a delay in the merger process would improperly harm Conrail and CSX.
Later, Norfolk Southern spokesman Bob Fort said the company would continue its legal case against the Conrail-CSX merger.
However, he said, "the decision obviously means that the stage is set for the (Conrail) shareholders meeting on Friday."
"From what we're hearing, we feel very optimistic about prevailing in the shareholders vote on Friday, and we look forward to being there."
